findings.summary: The Privacy Commissioner's Office found misuse of employers' personal data in loan applications and advised financial institutions to remain vigilant, without finding that a lender breached the PDPO or creating a new lender rule.
findings.title: Employers' data in loan applications: PCPD findings

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 26 August 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 PCPD has published findings on three loan-application cases in which foreign domestic helpers used employers’ personal data without consent. The findings were against the applicants, not financial institutions, but signal a control and conduct-risk review of third-party data in lending and collections journeys. Hong Kong 🟡 Employers’ data in loan applications: PCPD findings 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260825-pcpd-20260825-dpp3 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Lending, loan applications, collections The Privacy Commissioner’s Office found that three foreign domestic helpers contravened Data Protection Principle 3(1) by using employers’ names, residential addresses and/or telephone numbers for loan applications without prescribed consent, and issued warning letters to the helpers. The report says employers received debt contacts or overdue notices after defaults; one case involved four financial institutions. This is not a finding that any financial institution contravened the PDPO, and it does not create a new lender rule or deadline. PCPD says financial institutions should remain vigilant and avoid improper use of employers’ personal data in loan applications; lending and collections owners may use the findings as a risk-based trigger to assess how third-party data, consent and contact use are recorded and evidenced. Source: Privacy Commissioner’s Office Published a Report Relating to Three Cases Involving Misuse of Employers’ Personal Data by Foreign Domestic Helpers for Loan Applications Mainland/GBA SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. Watch List • Monitor any further PCPD publications on third-party personal-data handling in lending.
